1: **Russell** took pole and converted it to a dominant win — his first for Mercedes in 2026.
**Antonelli** finished 2nd on debut, showing immediate pace despite being a rookie.
**Leclerc (Ferrari)** took P3, giving Ferrari an early constructors' foothold.
McLaren struggled — both Norris and Piastri finished outside the top 5, raising early alarm bells.
Red Bull were off the pace throughout, signalling the RB22's troubled start to the new era.
2: **Antonelli** took his first career pole and converted it to his first race win in dominant fashion.
**Russell** finished P2, keeping Mercedes in a comfortable 1-2 formation.
**Hamilton** scored his first Ferrari podium — P3 — providing early encouragement for Maranello.
McLaren again struggled — pace deficit confirmed as a structural issue, not a one-race anomaly.
Verstappen finished outside the points; Red Bull described the car as undriveable in slow corners.
3: **Antonelli** took a second consecutive pole-to-win, extending his championship lead.
A timely safety car (debris incident) reset the race and fell perfectly for Antonelli's strategy.
**Piastri (McLaren)** took P2 — the first sign McLaren's upgrade trajectory was working.
**Leclerc** took P3 for Ferrari, but the team admitted Suzuka's high-speed layout masked their weaknesses.
Verstappen finished outside the points again — Red Bull's slow-corner deficit was starkly exposed at Suzuka's S-bends.
4: **McLaren's major upgrade package** arrived — Norris won Saturday's sprint, signalling a genuine performance step.
**Antonelli** made history: first driver ever to win their first four grands prix from pole position.
Early safety car (Hadjar-Gasly crash) reshuffled strategy; multiple lead changes throughout.
**Leclerc spun and hit the barrier** on the final lap fighting Piastri — earned a 20-second penalty, dropped from P3 to P8.
**Verstappen** spun from P2 on lap 1 but recovered to P5; Red Bull's upgrade showed improvement.
Wolff forced to intervene over team radio — first public hint of Mercedes internal tension.
5: **Russell** won Saturday's sprint from pole, cutting Antonelli's lead to 18 points and setting up a title fight narrative.
**McLaren gambled on intermediates** on a drying track at race start — catastrophic error. Piastri finished P11 two laps down; Norris DNF. "We looked like idiots" — Piastri.
**Russell vs Antonelli** produced a brilliant duel for the lead through the opening laps — multiple position swaps.
**Russell's power unit failed on lap 30** while leading — gifting Antonelli a clear run to victory.
**Hamilton** passed Verstappen into Turn 1 for P2 — his best Ferrari result of the season.
**Verstappen** took P3 — Red Bull's first podium of 2026.
6 retirements total: Russell (PU), Norris, Alonso, Albon, Pérez, Lindblad (DNS).
**Mercedes conceded** post-race they may need team orders to protect Antonelli's title lead — Wolff intervened on radio.
6: **Antonelli** took his 5th pole and 5th win of the season — dominant from lights to flag, crossing the line 6.3 seconds clear of Hamilton.
**Two standing restarts** — Lance Stroll crashed at Antony Noghes on lap 68, triggering a red flag. Track surface broke up at the site, requiring inspection before resuming.
**Verstappen retired on lap 1** with a power unit failure — his fourth DNF or points-less result of the season, continuing Red Bull's miserable chassis story despite having the best engine.
**Racing Bulls were sensational** — Hadjar P3 (2nd consecutive podium), Lawson P5, Lindblad P6. All three cars ahead of both Ferraris in the final classification.

**Gasly (Alpine)** crossed the line P3 but received two 5-second penalties for pitlane speeding — dropped to P7. Alpine have filed a Right of Review, claiming a pitlane lane-marking error caused drivers to inadvertently cut the lane.
**Russell P13** after two stewards' penalties — "a complete disaster I am struggling to comprehend." Now 68 points behind Antonelli.
**Leclerc DNF** — brake failure mid-race; described the SF-26 as "borderline dangerous" with 3 of 4 brakes not working. Ferrari furious.

**Cadillac denied their first point** — Pérez received a 10-second post-race penalty for being out of position at the restart, dropping from P10 to P15. **Alonso (Aston Martin) inherited P10** — their first point of 2026.
**ADUO confirmed:** Red Bull Powertrains/Ford declared the benchmark ICE — **Mercedes HPP and Ferrari now qualify for in-season upgrade opportunities**. Honda and Audi remain in 4%+ band.

**Result amended post-race:** Alpine's Right of Review was successful on Friday in Barcelona — FOM data showed the timing distance was inaccurate and overestimated Gasly's speed. **Gasly restored to P3**, Hadjar drops to P4, Piastri to P5. McLaren and Red Bull filed appeals against the reinstatement.
7: **Hamilton** claimed his 106th career win — first for Ferrari, first since the 2024 Belgian GP (686 days). Ferrari used an aggressive 3-stop strategy, exploiting a well-timed VSC caused by Alonso stopping at Turn 9.
**Russell** started from pole and led the early laps but was undercut by Hamilton at the second stop. He settled for P2, 19.5 seconds behind at the flag.
**First all-British podium since 1968** — Hamilton, Russell, Norris on the podium together for the first time ever.

**Antonelli retired on lap 62 of 66** with a Mercedes power unit failure, just after passing Russell for P2. Also given a post-race 5-second penalty for track limit violations — did not affect his retirement.
**Leclerc DNF** late in the race with a steering issue while running inside the top 5 — another missed points opportunity.
**Colapinto (Alpine)** crossed the line P8 but received a 10-second penalty for not slowing under yellow flags, dropping to P10. Lawson and Lindblad (Racing Bulls) elevated to P8 and P9.
**Alonso** started from pit lane (Aston Martin replaced ESME and MGU-K overnight) and finished outside the points.
Hamilton becomes the 7th oldest race-winner in F1 history at 41 years old.
8: **Russell** took pole despite Verstappen crashing in Q3 under yellow flags, then converted it to a controlled victory — his 7th career win, 2nd of 2026.
**Verstappen P2** — Red Bull's major upgrade package delivered its strongest showing of the season. Led from P5 on the grid after wheel-to-wheel battles with Hamilton in the opening laps.
**Antonelli P3** — a solid damage-limitation result after a messy opening phase where he ran wide multiple times. Chased Verstappen hard in the final lap but couldn't make Overtake Mode stick.
A VSC for **Sainz stopping on the main straight** (Williams electrical failure) caught Antonelli at the wrong moment — he had already pitted, missing the free stop.
**Hamilton P5** behind Piastri — Ferrari faded badly on tyre life. Leclerc P8 after struggling with deg throughout.
**Both Cadillacs retired early** (brake overheating) — Pérez and Bottas again failing to score despite Cadillac bringing their largest upgrade package yet.
**Alonso** given a 5-second penalty for pit lane speeding — finishing P18 classified.
Russell's championship deficit to Antonelli cut from 66 to **40 points** — the title fight is alive again.
**Led into summer break with Antonelli 50 pts clear of Hamilton. Post-break: Dutch GP won by Norris; Italian GP won by Antonelli from P19.**
9: **Sprint (Saturday):** Antonelli won his first-ever sprint race — youngest sprint winner in F1 history. Hamilton P2, Norris P3. Russell P4, Leclerc P5, Verstappen P6. Lawson took the final sprint point in P8.

**Race start drama:** Leclerc and Hamilton jumped Antonelli at the lights. Piastri and Lawson clashed on lap 1 — Piastri pitted with front wing damage and spent the rest of the race recovering. Albon tagged Bearman (10-second penalty) and later retired.

**Antonelli wheel shield failure (lap 41):** Leading after a long first stint, the Italian suffered a left-front wheel shield failure. Steering became compromised, leading to repeated track limit violations and a 5-second penalty. He finished P16 with zero points.
**Verstappen crashed at Stowe (lap 48)** while running P4 in contention for a podium, triggering the Safety Car. Race finished under the SC — Leclerc took his first 2026 victory without a restart.
**Russell pitted under the SC** from a slow puncture suffered earlier, leapfrogging Hamilton who stayed out. Race ended before a restart, costing Hamilton P2.
**Hamilton investigated post-race** for passing under yellow flags — stewards issued only a reprimand, P3 retained.
**Hadjar P5, Lawson P6, Lindblad P7** — Racing Bulls scored 14 points, one of their strongest team hauls of the season.
**Bortoleto P8** — Audi best result of 2026. Colapinto P9, Gasly P10 for Alpine.
**Championship impact:** Antonelli's lead cut from 40 to 25 points. Ferrari gained 51 points on Mercedes in a single weekend — the biggest constructors swing of 2026 so far.
10: **Antonelli from pole** — his 6th win of 2026, winning by 1.952 seconds over Leclerc.
**Verstappen stormed past through Eau Rouge on lap 1** using slipstream + Overtake Mode, briefly leading before Antonelli retook the position.
**Leclerc pitted under a VSC and briefly held the lead** — Antonelli closed and swept past at the Kemmel Straight on lap 34.
**Russell retired on lap 1** after contact with Hamilton at Raidillon — Mercedes accepted 100% blame. Second retirement in four races, now 50 pts behind Antonelli.
**Hamilton penalised 5 seconds** for the Russell collision, dropping from P3 to P4. Ferrari also fined €30k for unsafe pit release striking a mechanic.
**Norris, Hadjar, Alonso and Stroll all took grid penalties** for PU component changes, reshaping the grid dramatically.
**Piastri P5** from P9 on grid. **Lindblad P7**. Racing Bulls and Alpine now level on 80 constructor points.
**Championship: Antonelli +45 over Hamilton, +50 over Russell.** Summer break after Hungary — title drifting toward Antonelli.
11: **Norris from pole** — first 2026 win, 15 seconds clear of Verstappen. McLaren become the third constructor to win in 2026.
**Piastri led early** after jumping Norris off the line, McLaren resisting team orders. DNF on lap 60 with gearbox failure handed Norris a free run.
**Both Hamilton and Antonelli penalised 3 places in qualifying** — Hamilton for impeding Piastri, Antonelli for a yellow flag infringement. Grid reshuffled.
**Russell anti-stall failure off the start** dropped him from P6 to P19 on lap 1. Recovered to P7 but lost crucial title points. Now 59 behind Antonelli.
**Verstappen P2** — Red Bull second consecutive podium. Trademark late dive on Hamilton at Turn 1, lap 16.
**Antonelli P3** starting from P7 — charged through the field on a long opening stint, brilliant tyre management.
**Hamilton P5 after pit lane speeding penalty** — his fourth penalty in three races. Dropped from P4 behind Leclerc.
**Sainz-Piastri collision lap 39**: Piastri rejoined into Sainz at Turn 1. Sainz took 10-second penalty. Piastri's gearbox failure 20 laps later was unrelated.
**Hülkenberg P9** — Audi first double-points finish (Bortoleto P11). Lawson P8, Lindblad P10.
**Aston Martin B-spec showed promise**: Stroll P13, Alonso P14 — Newey upgrade beginning to work.
**Malaysia (Sepang) confirmed as R16** (Oct 2–4), hosting the Bahrain GP. Season extended from 22 to 23 races.
12: **Sprint (Saturday):** Russell won from pole, Hamilton P2, Norris P3. Antonelli P7 — a rare sprint off-day.
**Verstappen crashed heavily at the end of lap 1** in slippery conditions, losing the rear into Turn 12. Red-flagged. Verstappen unhurt, standing ovation from the home crowd.
**At the restart Antonelli made a lightning launch**, overtook Norris for P1 and stretched an 8-second lead through the middle stint on the hard tyre.
**Norris undercut with fresh mediums** and closed 1.5 seconds per lap. Retook the lead on lap 55 of 72 and pulled away to win by 11.536 seconds.
**Mercedes team orders late in the race** — Russell was asked to let Antonelli past for P2 to protect championship points. Russell complied but post-race: "I didn't have much choice."
**Hamilton P4, Leclerc P5** — Ferrari brought new front wing but couldn't challenge top 3.
**Lawson P7 for Red Bull** (after 10-second yellow flag penalty), deputising for the injured Hadjar. Tsunoda P11 for Racing Bulls in his one-off return.
**Penalty chaos:** Colapinto received a drive-through AND post-race 10 seconds. Sainz 10 seconds for collision with Albon. Lawson penalised. Lindblad drive-through — fell to P12.
**Hülkenberg P8, Alonso P9, Gasly P10** — Audi, Aston Martin and Alpine all scoring.
**Zandvoort confirmed removed from 2027 calendar** during the race weekend — this was the final Dutch GP.
**Mercedes admitted no upgrade budget** for rest of 2026. McLaren's development rate now impossible to match.
**Championship: Antonelli +49 over Hamilton, +68 over Russell, +100 over Norris.**
13: **Gasly takes Alpine's first-ever pole position** — historic moment for the team, their first pole since the Renault era.
**Antonelli started 19th** after taking a back-of-grid penalty for a new power unit — a strategic gamble by Mercedes given Monza's low-drag characteristics.

**Hamilton–Leclerc opening chicane battle**: Leclerc ran Hamilton off onto the gravel at the first chicane, sending him to 10th. Leclerc then crashed heavily at the exit of Parabolica on lap 3, red-flagging the race. Leclerc admitted it “went too far.”
**Standing restart**: Russell led from Gasly and Colapinto. Antonelli had climbed to P6 at the red flag and restarted P6.

**Antonelli's charge**: On fresher rubber and with superior energy deployment, Antonelli picked off cars lap by lap — Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Gasly, then finally Russell on lap 47 with a decisive move into the first chicane.
**Antonelli wins from 19th** — first driver since John Watson at the 1983 US Grand Prix West to win from 19th or below. First Italian to win the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.
**Russell P2** nursed aging tyres but couldn't hold Antonelli. **Verstappen P3** from P7 on the grid — back-to-back podiums for Red Bull.
**Norris P5, Piastri P4** — McLaren scored 22 points. Hamilton P6 after starting battle damage. **Ferrari scored zero constructors' points** — their worst day of 2026.
**Gasly P7** after leading early. Lindblad P8, Colapinto P9, Tsunoda P10 — first point of 2026 for the Racing Bulls substitute.
**Championship: Antonelli +66 over Russell, +75 over Hamilton.** Russell now P2 in the championship, having overtaken Hamilton.
14: **Norris on pole** at F1's inaugural Madring race — the first Spanish GP in Madrid since 1981. Colapinto P9 on the grid — the surprise of qualifying, out-qualifying Gasly by 5 places.
**Norris led from lights** and built a 6+ second gap over Antonelli in the opening stint. Looking dominant.

**VSC triggered on lap 16** when Stroll stopped at Turn 20 with brake issues. Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell all dived into the pits. Norris passed the pit entry one corner too late — unable to stop under VSC.

**Disaster for Norris:** forced to pit under green, suffered a sticky front-right — 7-second stop — and rejoined 5th behind all three VSC stoppers. He recovered to P3 but the win was gone. McLaren boss described it as 'cruel'.
**Antonelli won** from P2 on the grid, managing a car that felt 'unusual' late on and briefly touching the wall at Turn 7. First-ever F1 winner at the Madring.
**Verstappen P2** (+4.351s). **Norris P3** (+5.089s) — Red Bull and McLaren both ahead of Ferrari at a new circuit.
**Hamilton retired on lap 6** with a brake failure — his first DNF of the 2026 season. A devastating points loss. He is now 101 points behind Antonelli.
**Leclerc P4** after running long on the hard tyre and hoping for another safety car. Russell P5 despite two stops.
**Lawson P6, Colapinto P7, Piastri P8, Lindblad P9, Hülkenberg P10**. Racing Bulls scored a point in both cars. Audi now on 30 constructor points.

**DNFs:** Hamilton (lap 6, brakes), Stroll (lap 12, brakes), Pérez (lap 31), Sainz (lap 43). Sainz had also taken a 3-place grid penalty for impeding Bottas in qualifying — home heartbreak for the Madrid-born driver.

**The Madring circuit itself drew mixed reviews** — Fernando Alonso said 'it cannot continue this way'. Multiple drivers and teams criticised the lack of overtaking. F1 will need to evaluate future races at the venue.
**Championship: Antonelli +81 over Russell, +101 over Hamilton.** With 9 races left, Antonelli needs just 1 point to mathematically eliminate Hamilton.
